_comment: SCENARIO CATALOGUE — example / reference file
This file is the similarity input for the SimilarityBasedAdapter.
It contains two sections: monitored_parameters and scenarios.
Defines the numeric domain (type, min_value, max_value) of every variable
that may appear in any scenario condition (given / when / then).
The Jaccard similarity algorithm uses min_value and max_value to compute
interval lengths. If a variable is missing here, its Jaccard score is 0.
IMPORTANT — ASM parameter contract:
Any parameter that also exists in the Anticipated Scenario Model (asm.json)
MUST appear here with the EXACT SAME name and the SAME min_value/max_value
range. The similarity is calculated between the diagnosed scenario (whose
variables come from the ASM) and the catalogue candidates. If the name or
range differs, the pairing fails and the score drops to zero for that variable.
Note on format: asm.json uses 'min'/'max'; this file uses 'min_value'/'max_value'.
When copying ranges from the ASM, rename the keys accordingly.
Parameters are grouped into two categories:
[ASM] — mirrored from asm.json; name and range must stay in sync.
[CAT] — catalogue-only; variables used by candidate scenarios from other
applications that do not exist in the ASM.
Each candidate scenario represents a known situation from another robotic
application. It follows the same Given/When/Do/Then structure as the ASM.
STRATEGY — uniform 'when' across all candidates:
All candidates in this catalogue intentionally share the same 'when' condition
as the diagnosed scenario. This is NOT a requirement of the similarity algorithm
(which computes when_sim normally for any condition), but a deliberate design
choice that enforces a semantic constraint:
A candidate with a different 'when' represents a situation that cannot be
activated under the same conditions as the diagnosed scenario. Such a candidate
would be semantically inapplicable as an adaptation — even if its given/then
are similar. By pre-filtering the catalogue to candidates with the same 'when',
we guarantee that every ranked result is a valid adaptation option.
The practical effect: when_sim = 1.0 for all candidates, so 'when' contributes
a fixed 1/3 to every score and the ranking is driven entirely by given and then.
Similarity scores (against a diagnosed LIFT_OBJECT scenario):
lift_slip_low_friction   → ~0.99  HIGH   (same parameters, near-identical ranges)
cobot_lift_grip_pressure → ~0.61  MEDIUM (partial parameter overlap)
suction_arm_vacuum_loss  → ~0.33  LOW    (no shared parameters beyond 'when')
The minimum possible score is 0.33 because 'when' contributes a fixed 1/3
when all candidates share the same 'when' condition as the diagnosed scenario.

monitored_parameters._comment_asm: Parameters mirrored from asm.json — name and range MUST match exactly.
monitored_parameters._comment_cat: Catalogue-only parameters — used by candidate scenarios from other applications.

lift_slip_low_friction._comment: HIGH similarity (~0.99). Same parameters as a diagnosed LIFT_OBJECT failure — identical given/then structure, slightly wider lateral_friction threshold.
lift_slip_low_friction.name: Lift Slip — Low Friction Surface

cobot_lift_grip_pressure._comment: MEDIUM similarity (~0.61). Shares object_lift_height_cm with the diagnosed scenario; grip_pressure is a cobot-specific parameter not present in the ASM.
cobot_lift_grip_pressure.name: Cobot Lift Failure — Grip Pressure

suction_arm_vacuum_loss._comment: LOW similarity (~0.33). No shared parameters in given/then — all variables are suction-specific. Score is the minimum possible (1/3 from the shared 'when').
suction_arm_vacuum_loss.name: Suction Arm Lift — Vacuum Loss

parallel_arm_contact_loss._comment: HIGH similarity (~0.90). Same parameters as diagnosed given/then but without lateral_friction (this system has no friction sensor). Tversky penalty = 0.31 for the missing param; Jaccard on matched params = 1.0.
parallel_arm_contact_loss.name: Parallel Arm Lift — Contact Loss

lightweight_arm_height_only._comment: MEDIUM-HIGH similarity (~0.73). Same given as parallel_arm_contact_loss (given_sim = 0.69); then monitors only lift height (stricter threshold: >= 12cm), dropping finger_contacts — penalty = 0.47 on then, Jaccard = 0.98 on height.
lightweight_arm_height_only.name: Lightweight Arm Lift — Height Verification Only

heavy_duty_arm_motor_overload._comment: MEDIUM-LOW similarity (~0.50). Completely different given parameters (torque + temperature vs height + contacts + friction) — given_sim = 0. Then shares only object_lift_height_cm with the diagnosed; penalty = 0.50, Jaccard = 1.0 on height — then_sim = 0.50.
heavy_duty_arm_motor_overload.name: Heavy Duty Arm — Motor Overload During Lift
